summary: Comprehensive license analysis of all analyzed repositories and their dependencies

licenses.name: Apache License 2.0
licenses.notes: Highly permissive, widely used in enterprise. Patent grant provides additional protection. Only requires attribution and license file inclusion.

licenses.name: Community Specification License 1.0
licenses.notes: Used for specifications, not code. Implementation freedom guaranteed. Contributions to the specification have additional requirements (CLA). Does not restrict implementing the specification.

licenses.name: Eclipse Public License 2.0
licenses.notes: Weak copyleft - only modified EPL files must be shared, not the entire codebase. Compatible with Apache 2.0 in most cases. OSI-approved.

licenses.name: MIT License
licenses.notes: Very permissive, minimal restrictions. No patent grant unlike Apache 2.0, but still very safe for use.

licenses.name: BSD 3-Clause License
licenses.notes: Permissive license similar to MIT. Includes non-endorsement clause.

for_uml_codex.rationale: Most analyzed projects use Apache 2.0. Provides patent grant, widely understood in enterprise, compatible with all dependencies.
for_uml_codex.attribution_strategy: Create NOTICES.txt file listing all dependencies and their licenses. Include in distribution.
for_uml_codex.dependency_management: Track dependency licenses in project metadata. Automated license scanning recommended (pip-licenses, licensecheck).
compliance_checklist: Include Apache 2.0 LICENSE file in repository
Include copyright headers in source files (optional but recommended)
Document any modifications to Apache 2.0 dependencies
Ensure CI/CD includes license compliance checks

finos_cdm_specification.implication: Can freely implement the CDM specification. Cannot directly modify the specification itself without contributor agreement. For UML-Codex: reference CDM patterns and concepts, do not fork specification.

archived_repositories.implication: License remains valid despite archival. No ongoing support or security updates. Can use code but must maintain ourselves.

third_party_dependencies.summary: All third-party dependencies identified use permissive licenses (Apache 2.0, MIT, BSD-3-Clause) or weak copyleft (EPL 2.0). No GPL or strong copyleft licenses found.
